records.habit: Large stout perennial, distinctly four-sided erect stems 1–2.5 m
records.flowers: Calyx 2.5–3.5 mm or more; purple or lilac corolla tube slightly longer than calyx, limb ca. 2.5 mm across
records.regional_status_in_flora: Introduced from South America, spreading in north-central Texas
records.source_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Perennial from woody root, stems spreading to erect to 46 cm; foliage gray-pubescent
records.leaves: Lower blades typically narrow elongate oblong-lanceolate to spatulate, incised-dentate/pinnatifid; broadly margined or semi-clasping at base (flora key)
records.inflorescence: Floral bracts ovate, acuminate, typically slightly longer than calyx (flora key)
records.flowers: Calyx 2–3 mm; blue/lavender/purple corolla tube slightly longer than calyx; limb 4–6 mm across
records.source_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Erect perennial flowering first year, to 1 m
records.leaves: Few, petiolate, oblanceolate or obovate, toothed or lobed
records.inflorescence: Flowers becoming well spaced along axis
records.flowers: Calyx 3–3.5 mm; lavender-blue corolla rarely white, tube slightly longer than calyx; limb 6–7 mm across
records.taxonomy_note: Treat historical Verbena officinalis subsp. halei as a name crosswalk, not a reason to apply V. officinalis morphology.
records.source_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Coarse pubescent perennial with stems to 2 m
records.flowers: Calyx 3–4 mm; blue-purple corolla with tube about as long as calyx and limb 5–8 mm across
records.source_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.stems: Flower stalks with conspicuously long spreading hairs
records.inflorescence: Short stout spikes to ca. 4 cm long, 8–12 mm thick
records.flowers: Conspicuous corolla lobes; source key 2.7–4 mm, spreading to reflexed after flowering, bracts at base not keeled or clasping
records.diagnostic: Plant usually darkens conspicuously on drying; compare P. rhodosperma
records.source_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.inflorescence: Dense spikes to 20 cm long and ca. 10 mm thick; flower stalk hairs spreading at right angles (key)
records.flowers: Basal spike bracts keeled and clasping, bracts (2.2–)2.8–5.2(–5.4) mm; abaxial sepals acuminate with extended green midvein; corolla lobes 2–3 mm (key)
records.seeds: Red to reddish-black, (1.7–)2–2.8 mm, with transparent margin (source key)
records.habitat: Prairies, pastures, roadsides and disturbed sites
records.source_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Mat-forming succulent glabrous wetland perennial (source genus)
records.leaves: Opposite, sessile, spatulate, to ca. 20 mm, essentially entire; single prominent vein and wedge-shaped non-clasping base (key)
records.flowers: Axillary single flower per node on stalks to 25 mm with two narrow bracts below calyx; white to pale blue or lilac corolla 8–10 mm; genus 4 stamens
records.taxonomy_note: 1999 placed Bacopa in Scrophulariaceae; modern family Plantaginaceae under repository routing.
records.source_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Usually perennial; stems sprawling, decumbent or erect, to 100 cm
records.leaves: Opposite, sessile clasping oblong-lanceolate blades shallowly toothed
records.inflorescence: Axillary peduncled racemes often over 30 flowers (source key)
records.flowers: Pedicels 4–6(–8) mm; pale lavender to blue corolla 5–6 mm across
records.regional_status_in_flora: Historical flora labels introduced, native Europe and northern Asia
records.taxonomy_note: Modern family Plantaginaceae; historical flora treated Veronica in Scrophulariaceae. Historical nativity not a substitute for BONAP.
records.source_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Annual decumbent basally then ascending, up to 40 cm
records.inflorescence: Solitary axillary long-pedicelled flowers; pedicels 15–30 mm, often longer than leaves (source key)
records.taxonomy_note: Historical family Scrophulariaceae vs modern Plantaginaceae.
records.source_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Annual with prostrate/reclining stems to 30 cm
records.inflorescence: Solitary axillary flowers; fruiting pedicels 5–12 mm
records.flowers: Blue corollas 3–6 mm across; source key: usually blue throughout, unlike bicolored V. agrestis
records.fruits: Capsule lobes erect, glandular and eglandular hairs; style exceeding capsule notch (source key)
records.taxonomy_note: Jones et al. (1997) lumped V. polita with V. agrestis; 1999 flora retains distinct species. Family formerly Scrophulariaceae.
records.source_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
